author: Cornelius Nepos

passages.original: nam cum Byzantio expugnato cepisset complures Persarum nobiles atque in eis nonnullos regis propinquos, hos clam Xerxi remisit, simulans ex vinclis publicis effugisse, et cum iis Gongylum Eretriensem, qui litteras regi redderet, in quibus haec fuisse scripta Thucydides memoriae prodidit: 'Pausanias, dux Spartae, quos Byzantii ceperat, postquam propinquos tuos cognovit, tibi muneri misit seque tecum affinitate coniungi cupit: quare, si tibi videtur, des ei filiam tuam nuptum. id si feceris, et Spartam et ceteram Graeciam sub tuam potestatem se adiuvante te redacturum pollicetur.
passages.english: For when, after Byzantium had been taken by storm, he had captured a number of Persian nobles, and among them several relatives of the king, he secretly sent these back to Xerxes, pretending that they had escaped from the public prison, and with them Gongylus of Eretria, to deliver a letter to the king, in which, as Thucydides has recorded, the following was written: 'Pausanias, the commander of Sparta, has sent to you as a gift those whom he had captured at Byzantium, after he learned that they were your relatives, and he desires to be joined to you by marriage: therefore, if it seems good to you, give him your daughter in marriage. If you do this, he promises that, with your help, he will bring both Sparta and the rest of Greece under your power.
passages.notes: The final clause is grammatically odd: 'se adiuvante te' would literally mean 'he himself and you helping'; the sense is evidently 'with your help' (some editions read simply 'te adiuvante').
